subject: FINDING: latest-only hinge bridge can preserve stale close-cycle identity across a real reversal
body: WORKSTREAM_ID=ws-state-rd-hinge-ingress-edge-preservation-20261002. SOURCE-CONFIRMED on main 7a612a0fe3181768f548a1ec78d2c3ee5938a339: HingeAngleSource emits changed continuous angles on controlHandler; FoldOverlayService.enqueueHingeFromControl writes latestControlAngle and permits only one pending main runnable; intermediate control-thread samples are overwritten. Fold7ContinuityController uses the delivered sequence for Direction, 3-sample closing intent, closingFloor, opening reversal >=1.5 deg, threshold actions, and generation changes. Fold7Gen2Kernel invalidates a close cycle only when the controller actually transitions back to an open/handoff state. Therefore a physical open/re-close excursion entirely inside one pending main window can be erased. Concrete modeled source-faithful case: state COVER_PREWARMING, last/floor=130, original closeCycle=1, raw burst 135 then 128. Full delivery observes reversal, releases secondary, ends cycle 1, then re-close creates cycle 2 and re-enters PREWARMING at generation+3. Current latest-only delivery sees only 128, remains PREWARMING at the old generation with closeCycle=1 still accepted. Separate deterministic case: OPEN_INNER 179 with raw 178/177/176/175 proves deliberate closing under the controller's 3-sample/3-degree rule; latest-only sees only 175 (4-degree delta, below strong-sample 5 degrees) and remains OPEN_INNER. This is a control-plane semantic loss, not merely animation-frame dropping. Adjacent semantic-reclose workstream owns missing DeviceState OPEN->CLOSED callbacks; this finding is precise-angle ingress after those samples already exist.
